analysis.title: Best Buy Co. (BBY): First Take: 3Q27 beat driven by tariff refund, FY27 guidance raised
key_insights: BBY reported 3Q27 adj. EPS of $1.62 vs GS est $1.47 and consensus $1.49. Enterprise comp sales +6.1% y/y vs GS +1.0% and consensus +2.3%.
The beat was helped by $41mn of tariff refunds. GS estimates ex-refund gross margin ~23.5%, adj. EBIT margin ~4.0% and EPS ~$1.47, in line with GS estimate.
Domestic online comps +10.8% y/y and 33.2% of domestic sales vs 31.8% a year ago.
Domestic adj. SG&A grew 8.1% y/y vs GS +2.7%, on incentive compensation and Marketplace and Best Buy Ads investment.
Inventory +11.4% y/y vs sales +5.8%. Payables ratio rose to 96.1% from 91.6%.
FY27 guidance raised: revenue $43.0bn-$43.3bn, comps +3.4%-4.0%, adj. EBIT margin ~4.5%, adj. EPS $6.90-$7.05, all at or above consensus.
4Q27 guide: comps +2.0%-4.0% vs consensus +2.3%, adj. EBIT margin 4.9%-5.1% vs consensus 5.0%. Roughly in line.
GS stays Sell with a $71 12-month PT (5.0x/6.0x/6.5x EV/EBITDA), 26.8% below the $97 price. Stock is up pre-market.
Call focus: memory pricing and inventory availability, AUR and elasticity, QTD trends, FY28 momentum, promotions, Marketplace and Ads investment.

market_movers.rationale: Beat was aided by $41mn tariff refunds, and ex-refund EPS was ~$1.47, in line with GS. GS sees 26.8% downside to the $71 PT.

earnings_insights: 3Q27 adj. EPS $1.62 reported (adjusted) vs GS est $1.47 and consensus est $1.49 (FactSet). Ex $41mn tariff refunds GS estimates EPS ~$1.47.
3Q27 sales $10.236bn reported, +5.8% y/y, vs GS est $9.756bn and consensus est $9.886bn.
3Q27 adj. EBIT margin 4.4% reported vs GS/consensus est 4.2%/4.2%. Ex refunds ~4.0%.
4Q27 guidance: comps +2.0%-4.0% (consensus est +2.3%), adj. EBIT margin 4.9%-5.1% (consensus est 5.0%).
FY27 guidance raised to adj. EPS $6.90-$7.05 from $6.70-$6.90 prior (consensus est $6.82). Capex unchanged at $750mn.
GS FY27 EPS est $6.73 (1/27E) and FY28E $7.16, pre-update.
risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell: pull-forward purchases and tax refunds, better memory supply mitigation, Marketplace and Ads offsetting memory margin pressure, trade-up to premium devices, housing recovery, share gains, product innovation.
Quality of beat: tariff refunds are non-recurring, SG&A growth is above plan and inventory is outpacing sales.
